name: DeepSEA
baseline_reconsider_when: Reconsider only under a written historical-exception policy with the original artifact correctly identified.
assessment: Condition not met on either part, and the artifact part has got worse since August. (1) Policy: Foundation_models/MAINTENANCE.md (file mtime 2026-07-14) still requires a model to be 'pretrained, reusable, and broader than one task' and contains no historical or canonical exception clause. UNDER_REVIEW.md still names the missing policy as the blocker. (2) Original artifact: the release page found in August at deepsea.princeton.edu/help/ now returns HTTP 404 over http and 503 over https, and the site root serves a default Rocky Linux 'HTTP Server Test Page' (403). The lab's live server, HumanBase DeepSEA, offers Sei (2021) and Beluga (2019) but not the 2015 919-feature model, and Sei is already displayed as bfm-sei. Selene (BSD-3-Clause-Clear) contains a DeepSEA architecture definition (models/deepsea.py) and manuscript case-study scripts, not the original trained release. Note for the curator: the displayed catalog already includes supervised multi-task sequence-to-function predictors (Enformer, Borzoi, Sei, Orca), and DeepSEA is closer to those precedents than ChromBPNet is. The recorded condition still needs a written decision, which no external evidence can supply. If that policy is adopted and no official copy of the 2015 weights can be reached, retiring this record in favour of bfm-sei is a better fit than displaying it without an artifact. A third-party G3 2026 paper (Maillard, Demars, Mourad) reuses DeepSEA for cross-species annotation. That shows continued use but does not bear on the condition.
evidence_boundary: Condition-focused re-review. The Nature Methods page gives the abstract only (full text paywalled), so the inherited '919 features' and '~1 kb input' claims were not re-verified today. The Wayback Machine availability API returned HTTP 429 (shared rate limit), so whether an archived copy of the original release page exists is unchecked. The HumanBase 'Downloads' section and the Kipoi DeepSEA entry (a third-party model zoo, lead only) were not opened. No model files were downloaded.

name: ChromBPNet
baseline_reconsider_when: Reconsider if a written scope policy includes assay-specific predictors or broader reusable pretraining is evidenced.
assessment: Condition not met. (1) There is still no written scope policy covering assay-specific predictors (MAINTENANCE.md unchanged). (2) No broader reusable pretraining is evidenced. The preprint was revised after September: v3 posted 2026-09-22 and v4 posted 2026-09-23, still not journal-published according to the bioRxiv API, with an unchanged abstract. The v4 full text presents ChromBPNet as a lightweight model trained on each dataset. It contrasts this with fine-tuning large pretrained models and mentions sequence-anchored 'foundation' models only as a future direction. The reusable artifacts are: MIT code (release v1.0.1, 2025-07-11; last push 2026-06-09); a CC-BY-4.0 Zenodo deposit by Pampari, Shcherbina and Kundaje (2022-12-10) containing reference enzyme-bias models (bias_models.zip, about 16.6 MB) that the README says transfer within an assay type; and many per-dataset trained ChromBPNet models on the ENCODE portal and Synapse, as stated in the preprint. Together these make a per-dataset training recipe with a transferable bias component, not one broadly pretrained model. Unlike Enformer, Sei or Borzoi (one model covering many tasks), even a future supervised-predictor exception would need to say whether compendia of per-dataset checkpoints count.
evidence_boundary: Condition-focused review of the v4 preprint full text (bioRxiv JATS), README, licence, releases and the Zenodo bias-model record. The ENCODE portal model files and Synapse project (syn59449898) were not opened, so their terms are not checked. No checkpoint was downloaded or executed. The year stays 2024 (first preprint), although the official Zenodo data deposit dates from 2022-12-10 and the repository was created 2021-07-23. That is a curator call if the record is ever promoted.

name: Mistral-DNA
baseline_reconsider_when: Reconsider when a primary source, authorized checkpoint, direct model card, and exact terms are all verified.
assessment: Three of the four sub-conditions are now met; the primary source is still missing. Authorized checkpoint: met. The developer's Hugging Face account (RaphaelMourad) lists 15 public, ungated Mistral-DNA-v1 checkpoints (1M-422M parameters; hg38 plus bacteria, yeast, Arabidopsis, lncRNA, bacteriophage, plasmid, virus, noncoding and three livestock-breed sets), with safetensors weights. Direct model card: met (e.g., v1-422M-hg38 and v1-17M-hg38: a 'pretrained generative DNA sequence model', derived from a reduced Mixtral-8x7B and pretrained on 10 kb hg38 sequences). Exact terms: weights carry apache-2.0 in the card metadata of the three hg38 cards checked. The GitHub repository has no licence file (API 404; licence null), so the code has no stated licence. Primary source: not met. Europe PMC ('Mistral-DNA': 5 hits, all third-party benchmarks or reviews), the arXiv API (0 hits) and one web search found no paper, preprint or technical report. The closest developer-authored documents are Galaxy Training Network tutorials (Mourad & Batut; CC-BY-4.0; pretraining tutorial published 2025-04-17, revised 2026-07-13). They use v1-17M-hg38 for fine-tuning and zero-shot prediction but do not document how the released v1 checkpoints were trained or evaluated. Drift: the README still points to RaphaelMourad/Mistral-DNA-v0.1, which returns HTTP 401 (not public); the record should link the v1 checkpoints instead. Curator's call: the catalog accepted an official release write-up in place of a paper for MarinDNA. If developer tutorials plus model cards are judged sufficient as primary documentation, the proposed_record below is ready for promotion as verified_with_limits.
evidence_boundary: Licence metadata and file listings were checked for 3 of the 15 v1 checkpoints (17M, 138M and 422M hg38); the other 12 were seen only in the author listing (ungated, public). The repository notebooks were not executed and no weights were downloaded. The scale of third-party reuse (GUANinE v1.1, the 'DNA dialect' review) comes from Europe PMC result titles only. The WebSearch result (a Medium post describing v0.1) is a lead and was not used as evidence.

name: HybriDNA
baseline_reconsider_when: Reconsider when a provenance-confirmed official reusable model artifact is released and verified.
assessment: Condition met, with limits. September's blocker was that no author-controlled link established who owned the Mishamq uploads. Today I found that link. (1) The first author controls the GitHub account Mamingqian: that account owns mamingqian.github.io (GitHub Pages), and the site states he worked on HybriDNA as a Microsoft Research AI for Science intern. (2) The same account's repository Mamingqian/HybriDNA (created 2026-01-15) carries the arXiv citation and links all three Hugging Face checkpoints (300M, 3B, 7B) and the Mishamq HybriDNA collection. (3) The Mishamq profile's full name is Mingqian Ma, and its organisations are umich and CladeTeam. Both match the author's own site: a BSE from the University of Michigan, and CENO released through a CladeTeam collection. This resolves August's objection that the organisations did not match. (4) Artifact identity: the hidden size and layer counts in the config.json of each repository match Table 7 of arXiv v2 exactly (7B: 32 layers/4096; 3B: 16/4096; 300M: 24/1024). The 3B card body still says 'This is the 300M parameter variant'. That is a copy error in the card; the 3B config and sharded safetensors are consistent with the paper's 3B model. (5) Access: all three repositories are ungated, list safetensors weights, and declare apache-2.0 in their metadata. Remaining limits, carried in audit_note: no Microsoft organisation release (the project page's microsoft/HybriDNA link still returns 404); the author's own HybriDNA publication page does not link the weights; the GitHub companion has only a README and requirements, with an Apache badge but no LICENSE file; whether the uploads are the exact paper checkpoints rests on the author's statement; no journal version exists (arXiv v2, 2025-02-18, is the latest). Interpretation choice for Michaela: I read 'official' as released by a paper author through accounts the author verifiably controls, because the institutional locator has been dead since at least August. If she requires a Microsoft organisation release, this becomes keep_hold with the same evidence. Lead outside this batch: the same first author lists CENO, a genome-scale model released at WAIC 2026 with code and open checkpoints. I did not verify it.
evidence_boundary: Checked today: arXiv API and v2 HTML full text (affiliations, Table 7, benchmark sentence); the project page HTML; microsoft/HybriDNA through the GitHub API and HTML (both 404); GitHub search for 'HybriDNA'; the Mamingqian/HybriDNA README and repository API; repository metadata for the author's personal site; the author's site home page and HybriDNA publication page; Hugging Face API for all three repositories, the user overview and collections; raw README for all three cards and config.json for all three. Europe PMC and Crossref show no journal version. Not checked: no weights downloaded or run; no confirmation from Microsoft; the GO-CRE preprint (same author) was not read to see whether it uses these checkpoints; the Hugging Face remote-code files were not audited.

name: SPgen
baseline_reconsider_when: The repository adds an explicit licence and ships downloadable SPgen checkpoints, or an author-controlled model-hub or Zenodo artifact appears, or a peer-reviewed version documents released weights. Re-verify licence wording at that point.
assessment: The licence half of the condition is now met. License.md (MIT, 'Copyright (c) [2026] [Jiachen Li]') was added on 2026-09-13 (commit 2716a92), and GitHub detects MIT. The weights half is not met. The repo tree has 11 files and none is a checkpoint. There are no releases. The README states that model_weights.pth is written by the user's own SP_demo.py training run. No author-controlled Hugging Face or Zenodo artifact turned up (the HF 'SpGen' hits are unrelated 2024 repos). The preprint is still v1 and unpublished. I recommend retirement because of scope, not terms. The preprint Methods say 'For each dataset, SPgen is trained on the training set for 8,000 epochs'. Spot embeddings are learned by a GAT on each tissue's own spatial graph. Evaluation is a protein-level holdout within each dataset, and no cross-dataset transfer is reported. The pretrained components are third-party scGPT, ESM-1b and PubMedBERT, used as frozen encoders. SPgen is therefore a per-dataset training method for one task (spatial protein imputation). MAINTENANCE.md puts that out of scope ('methods without a reusable pretrained artifact', 'single-task predictors'). Releasing the per-dataset checkpoints named in the current reconsider_when would not change this, so the hold has no exit that could make the record in scope. The retirement is reversible. If Michaela prefers to keep the hold, the fallback reconsider_when is: the authors release a pretrained SPgen model documented to run on new tissues or datasets without retraining, with explicit weight terms. Minor: the preprint's Code Availability Statement says 'TSvelo is implemented in Python' (a copy-paste slip) but links the correct SPgen repo.

name: JUMP-lite (with Nahual)
baseline_reconsider_when: An unsigned listing of the Cell Painting Gallery publication_data / images prefixes for the JUMP-lite release returns objects, i.e. the metadata bundle, embeddings and image stores are actually downloadable; re-verify the data licence at that point.
assessment: Condition met on 2026-10-10. Unsigned S3 listings of the public cellpainting-gallery bucket now return: the metadata/v1.0 bundle with 7 objects (README, site index, image index, perturbation metadata, RefChemDB annotations, plate manifest, metadata_manifest.json); four image stores (zstd, jpegxl_lossy_hq, _mq, _d20) under images/jump_lite_v1.0/images_compressed/; 16 embedding variant prefixes under workspace_dl/embeddings/<model>-<codec>/jump_lite/v1.0/; cell and nuclei mask stores; and Target-2 manifests and object features. Unsigned GETs of the metadata README (12,791 bytes), metadata_manifest.json (site_count 655101) and a .zgroup, plus HEAD requests for a zstd zarr.json and an embedding parquet, all returned 200. Data licence re-verified: the Cell Painting Gallery is CC0 1.0 per the AWS Open Data registry; the JUMP-lite README defers data terms to the gallery and JUMP, and the Zenodo index tables are CC0. Code is MIT (GitHub; Zenodo v1.0 and v1.1 archives). Two caveats that do not block promotion: (a) the paths documented in both the GitHub README and the in-gallery README (images/2026_jump_lite_v1.0/..., embeddings .../2026_jump_lite_v1.0/) return KeyCount 0; the data sit at images/jump_lite_v1.0/ and .../jump_lite/v1.0/; (b) the GitHub README still says the release is 'awaiting gallery promotion'. Correction to September: that review listed with max-keys=1, so 'one object (README.md)' was an artefact of the query; the image index parquet already carries LastModified 2026-09-02. September did correctly find the compressed-image prefix empty, because it queried the documented path. Scope: benchmark modality; JUMP-lite is a dataset/benchmark and Nahual is deployment tooling. Neither is a pretrained model, which fits the 'benchmark' route in MAINTENANCE.md.
evidence_boundary: Sampled listings (max-keys 3-200) and small-file GETs only; no image stores or embedding sets were downloaded and full object counts (655,101 sites x 16 embedding variants) were not verified. Did not assess whether licences of upstream embedding models (e.g. OpenPhenom, SubCell) impose terms on the released embedding outputs. The CPG CC0 statement is the gallery-wide registry licence; there is no JUMP-lite-specific data licence file. Nahual licence status comes from a GitHub licence API 404 and a pyproject.toml without a licence field.
